page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor technology. The system features 64 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, operating on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor clocked at 2.7 GHz. Memory capacity totals 256 GB of system RAM, establishing a 1:4 ratio of vCPU to memory (4.0 GB per vCPU). Hardware cache specifications include 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache per core. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI, VAES, and SHA_NI acceleration. The instance includes a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero local disk storage, and no GPU hardware accelerators.

Benchmark evaluation shows strong multi-threaded performance in the top 25% tier for multi-core stress testing, Geekbench multi-core scoring, PassMark CPU total score, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and PassMark database operations. In contrast, single-core CPU metrics, including single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, rank in the middle 50% average performance band. Memory bandwidth measurements for both small cached blocks and large uncached read/write blocks also remain in the middle 50% average range. Inference speeds for small 135M parameter LLM models achieve top 25% throughput, whereas medium 7B model inference rates fall within the middle 50% tier.

The absence of integrated local storage and GPU hardware reduces unnecessary resource overhead for memory-balanced parallel compute workloads. The 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers predictable scaling density for multi-threaded server environments that rely on external block storage. Suitable workloads include parallel software build systems, database engines, backend enterprise microservices, micro-batch ETL pipelines, and concurrent web application deployments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8369B processor with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores. It provides 256 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, along with a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance features no local storage or GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded performance in the top 25% for tasks such as parallel software compilation, multi-core CPU stress tests, PassMark database operations, and encryption tests, while single-core processing and memory bandwidth fall into the middle 50% average range. Without bundled local disk costs or GPU overhead, it offers qualitative resource density for parallel compute tasks. This configuration is suitable for database operations, backend enterprise applications, software build environments, and containerized microservices.
